title: I Grabbed the Balloon Nobody Can Let Go Of 🎈
lines: At the parade, a kid let go of his balloon and I caught the string.
His dad shook my hand for a full minute.
Thank you. He's been holding that since kindergarten.
I swept the street after the parade. I was reaching for a gum wrapper.
The kid ran off to finally have a childhood.
The balloon looked down at me.
Then it went up. So did I.
By noon I was over the stadium. They were doing the wave. I did it too.
A news helicopter pulled up next to me. The pilot leaned out.
Over Canada, a goose joined me. It wasn't going my way. It came anyway.
Over the ocean, a cruise ship threw me a sandwich. It was a great throw.
In London, I sat on top of Big Ben for one minute. It was a long minute.
In Paris, a mime pretended to pull me down. It almost worked.
I let go with one hand. The balloon held on with both.
I tied the string to a truck. Now I have a truck.
I asked a bird to pop it. The bird asked for a ride.
I ate breakfast in a cloud. I paid rent to a weather balloon.
Then I figured out the rule.
The kid never let go because he was tired.
He let go because somebody laughed at the parade.
The balloon only lets go when someone laughs harder than the person holding it.
Nobody had laughed at that kid in twenty years.
So I needed one laugh. From a mile up.
I spelled jokes with geese. Nobody looked up.
Then I heard drums. The parade. One year later.
I came down over row one. Beard full of birds. A goose on my head. A truck on my string.
A little girl looked up at me.
She laughed so hard she dropped her ice cream.
The balloon let go. I fell into a tuba.
The string landed in her hand.
She wasn't scared. She was eight. It was the best day of her life.
Her dad grabbed the string to stop her.
His daughter shook his hand for a full minute.
He's somewhere over Iceland now. Every morning she waves.
Every morning, a goose waves back.
